samples.summary: Design doc still states the paste merge-refusal contract with only the single-cell exemption; the new cut exemption is unrecorded
samples.evidence: docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:103-108 says "A paste that would only partially overwrite a block is refused whole (`merge-paste-partial`...); a single-cell destination is exempt, since it writes through the merge anchor." After this delta a second exemption exists — a cut's own travelling blocks are filtered out of the split check (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2429-2437) — so the design doc now describes the previous contract. The task doc records the decision (docs/tasks/active/20260912-sheets-paste-merge-propagation-todo.md:56-61) and its own plan item 'Update docs/design/sheets/sheet.md (copy/paste bullet)' (line 81) is already checked, so the doc update was missed. Fix belongs in the doc.

samples.summary: Split-refusal is now suppressed based on a stale copy-buffer snapshot; nothing invalidates copyBuffer.merges between cut and paste
samples.evidence: The new `travelling` set is built from `this.copyBuffer.merges` (sheet.ts:2431-2437), a snapshot taken at cut time. `copyBuffer` is only ever cleared explicitly (sheet.ts:2138-2140, 2284) — `unmergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4679-4713), `mergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4658) and the row/column structural ops (sheet.ts:1245, 1253) never invalidate or re-map it. So after a cut, a user (or a remote collaborator over yorkie-store) can unmerge/re-merge so that a block currently anchored at a stale source anchor spans into the destination region; that block is then excluded from the `isRangeInRange` split check even though it is a live destination block, and it is instead deleted wholesale by the cut branch's `replacedMerges` push (sheet.ts:2276-2282) using the stale span. A refusal the guard is supposed to raise is skipped and a destination block disappears silently. To confirm: exercise cut → unmerge/merge at the same anchor with a wider span → paste at an overlapping destination. Fix belongs on the new code (validate travelling anchors against the current merge map, or invalidate the copy buffer on merge-map changes).

verdict.reason: The described code is present as claimed. `planPasteMerges` excludes anchors from the stale copy-buffer snapshot from the split-refusal check (sheet.ts:2432-2440); the snapshot is taken at cut time (sheet.ts:2172, 2194-2200) and is invalidated only by explicit clearing (sheet.ts:2138-2140, 2284). `mergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4658-4660) and `unmergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4696-4700) mutate the live merge map without touching `copyBuffer`, and both are reachable from the UI while a cut buffer is live (view/worksheet.ts:5174-5184, view/spreadsheet.ts:563-569) — no clearCopyBuffer on those paths (only post-paste at view/worksheet.ts:4938, view/spreadsheet.ts:725, and Escape at view/worksheet.ts:5105-5112). Hence cut → unmerge → re-merge wider at the same anchor → paste bypasses the refusal at sheet.ts:2438, and the cut branch deletes the live (wider) block by anchor using the stale span (sheet.ts:2276-2282 → applyPasteMerges sheet.ts:2471-2480), silently destroying a destination block and under-scoping changedSrefs. No guard elsewhere prevents this; the design doc (docs/tasks/active/20260912-sheets-paste-merge-propagation-todo.md:41-44) addresses only layout reproduction, not the travelling-anchor staleness. Real, reachable, and major under the blast-radius rubric (invariant other entry points violate / guard with a reachable bypass).

finding.summary: Paste-created merges bypass the freeze-pane guard that every other merge-creation path honours, violating the invariant documented at docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:253 and assumed by the renderer
finding.evidence: The only existing merge-creation entry point, `mergeSelection`, refuses a block crossing the freeze boundary via `canMergeSelection` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4591-4599: `crossesFrozenRows`/`crossesFrozenCols`). `docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:253` states "Merges that cross freeze pane boundaries are disallowed." The new `planPasteMerges` (sheet.ts:2390) translates the copied blocks by the paste delta and creates them with no freeze check, so with `frozenCols=2` copying a merged D1:E1 and pasting at B1 yields a B1:C1 block straddling the boundary. The renderer relies on the invariant: `packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:1917` `toCellRect` computes the merged rect from a single scrolled origin, so a straddling block is drawn with the wrong rect across the frozen pane (the same hole exists in `moveRangeTo`, which is also unguarded, but this change adds a second reachable path). Fix belongs in `planPasteMerges`/`applyPasteMerges`.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding is present as described. `canMergeSelection` enforces the freeze-boundary rule (sheet.ts:4602-4610) and is the gate for `mergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4629); `docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:253` states merges crossing freeze panes are disallowed. `planPasteMerges` (sheet.ts:2391-2450) translates copied merge anchors by the paste delta (2415-2418) with only a split check (2438) and no frozenRows/frozenCols consultation, and `applyPasteMerges` writes them directly via store.setMerge (2482-2484). A grep of frozenRows|frozenCols across sheet.ts shows the merge-related use exists only in canMergeSelection, confirming the paste path bypasses it; `paste` (2214-2296) adds no freeze guard either, and `setFreezePane` (512-515) permits freeze with no merge validation, so a frozen sheet plus an internal paste of merged blocks is reachable. The renderer genuinely assumes the invariant: gridcanvas renders per freeze quadrant with distinct scroll origins (gridcanvas.ts:205-400) while `toCellRect` (1917-1940) builds the merged rect from one anchor origin, and covered cells are skipped (774-776, 1900-1910), so a straddling block renders wrong. No guard elsewhere makes it unreachable, and the invariant is one another module reads — in-lane for blast radius at major severity. The pre-existing identical hole in moveRangeTo (sheet.ts:2577) does not refute it, and per instructions I do not judge whether the diff introduced the code.
